storm.summary_layperson: No storms anywhere nearby tonight — a calm, dry autumn evening under high pressure, with nothing for the Sound to help or hurt.
storm.local_effect_blurb: Air–water gap is already down to 4°F at 4 PM and the air drops below the 60°F Sound by 6 PM — no marine-layer buffer this evening, but none is needed.
storm.detail_html:
Regional picture: Strong high pressure (about 1032 hPa) is parked over the area. KOKX radar shows no echoes at all, there are no NWS watches, warnings, or advisories, and the model shows zero instability (CAPE 0 J/kg) with weak wind shear aloft (11 kt). There is nothing to grow a thunderstorm tonight.

Local modifier: On warm days the cool Sound builds a stable marine layer that often weakens storms before they reach the cove. That isn't in play tonight. The Sound is 60°F against 64°F air inland — a 4°F gap, already under the ~5°F needed for a meaningful buffer. The Sound holds its temperature while the air cools after sunset (5:58 PM), so the gap closes and then reverses: by 6 PM the air is forecast near 57°F and by 7 PM about 55°F, colder than the water.

Cove vs surrounding areas: Same as everyone else — dry and quiet. With no storms around, the missing marine layer doesn't matter tonight.

What would change the call: Only a new echo appearing on radar, which nothing in the data supports. The next storm-relevant change would come with the next frontal system, not this evening.

wind.regime_label: Light gradient wind — no sea breeze, direction may wander

hourly.shift_note: sunset lull, near calm, direction unreliable

wind.tactics_blurb: A drifter around sunset, then a light breeze refills from the SSE and swings steadily right to SW. After 7 PM, go toward the right and expect the shifts to keep coming the same way rather than swinging back.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
The call: light gradient wind, no sea breeze. The cove is reading a light SSW of 5 kt (RYC 10-minute average 4.5 kt), and the southerly is everywhere — inland White Plains, the south shore of Long Island, Block Island — which marks it as background (gradient) flow around the big high, not a sea breeze. The thermal never got going today: the air–water temperature difference is only 4°F (64°F inland vs 60°F Sound), well under what drives a real sea breeze in late October, so there is no sea-breeze collapse to wait for and the sea-breeze direction correction does not apply.

Sunset lull (5–6:30 PM). Sunset is 5:58 PM. Both recent model runs show the wind dying to 1–3 kt and briefly backing to the east around 6 PM as the land cools. An east wind is the cove's worst direction — Greenwich Point shelters the course — so expect a near-drifter on the line around sunset, with puffs of 3–4 kt at best.

Refill and veer (7–10 PM). By 7 PM the breeze refills from the SSE at about 5 kt, then swings steadily clockwise: SSW around 8 PM, SW by 9, WSW by 10, holding about 6 kt. This is a persistent shift, not an oscillation — the wind rotates one way and doesn't come back. While it's still SSE, Greenwich Point shades the east side of the course and pressure favors the west side. Once it settles into SSW–SW it fills the cove fairly evenly, slightly stronger toward the mouth.

Model vs observations: The latest model run shows the wind at SSE (164°) for the 4 PM hour while stations around the western Sound show S (190°) — a 26° gap. In this light gradient wind that's ordinary wander, not a sea-breeze signal. Regional direction agreement is only 64%, and the Old Greenwich and Port Chester waterfront stations read near calm, so expect the direction to wander in the lighter patches.

What racers will feel: 2–6 kt all evening. That's light-air technique for most boats — heavier keelboats may struggle to hold steerage through the sunset lull, and dinghies will be on the edge of planing only in the best puffs after 8 PM. Play the persistent right shift: tack toward the new wind rather than waiting for a header that won't come.

data_caveats: Latest model run (19Z) was still publishing and stopped at 7 PM; the 8–10 PM wind rows come from the previous run (18Z), which matched the latest run within 1–2 kt and 15–25° where the two overlap.
Model gives no gust values; gusts are estimated at about 2 kt above sustained speed.
Western Sound buoy 44040 reading is 75 minutes old.
Sound water temperature from Bridgeport Harbor (BRHC3).
Wind direction agreement across stations is only 64% and waterfront stations near the cove read near calm — direction confidence is moderate in these light winds.
